scope: Local implementation of slice S3b of docs/QR_2_PORTFOLIO_PERFORMANCE_CONTRACT.md (RC-Q35, RC-Q36): the per-Bot performance route reads its snapshot on the main thread and computes the view in one long-lived worker thread per process (deadline 10000 ms; limits 256 MB old generation, 32 MB young generation, 4 MB stack); a timeout, crash, heap or spawn failure answers 503 QR2_REPORT_FAILED with Retry-After 2 and the next request starts a new worker. The route stays behind QR2_PERFORMANCE_ENABLED, which is off everywhere.
method: An architecture auditor (Opus 5.5) wrote the S3b design and root decided RC-Q35. A coder (Sonnet 5.5) wrote S3b; an independent architecture auditor (Opus 5.5) reviewed rounds 1 and 2; an independent tester (Sonnet 5.5) ran single-edit mutations after each of three rounds and the measurement at the read limit. Root ruled on every finding. A sole-runner tester then ran, with nothing else active, every test file that imports a changed module of the three slices of this wave (found with git grep): 54 PostgreSQL files one file per process on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster (804 tests, 0 fail; 3 skipped by environment gates in files this wave did not change: one non-loopback address check and two TEMP-privilege suites), the full unit suite (2150 tests, 0 fail, 6 skipped by platform gates, 9 todo) and the grant text test. Two later test-only assertions (one QR-3 reader case and one S3b import-scanner case) were checked by an independent tester (Sonnet 5.5) with their target mutations, both killed. Nobody verified their own work.
hashNote: SHA-256 of the line-feed content as Git stores it.
result: qr2-compute-pool 29 of 29, qr2-compute-http 5 of 5 and qr2-route-http 21 of 21 pass with 0 skipped; the S2 reader files pass unchanged. Measurement (RC-Q36): with the worker the longest event-loop delay was 38.5 ms (F1) and 42.6 and 46.2 ms (F2), against inline stalls of about 3.7 s; a parallel cheap request p95 about 1.1 ms; F2 route p95 3859 ms in one run and 4443 ms in the other against the 4237 ms bar, both below 5 s.

mutations.round1: 7 of 8 killed; the survivor zeroes read_ms, a timing field with no deterministic assertion.
mutations.round3: 1 of 2 killed; the import-scanner survivor became a test and was killed in the later check.

limits: The F2 route p95 bar (S3a p95 plus 300 ms) is not reliably met on this machine: one of two runs passed.
A 512 MB old-generation limit was about 2.3 times slower; the cause was not investigated.
The route stays off everywhere; before it is turned on, the target server is measured again and its memory headroom is read.
Measured on Windows with Node 24 only; no staging or VPS measurement.

rootAcceptance.statement: Root reviewed the agent reports, the rulings, the sole-runner verification and the final diff and accepted S3b as local engineering evidence for the QR-2 row. Acceptance changes no PM-1 credit by itself and deploys nothing.
